OpenAI is rolling out a chat-tuned version of GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT's Chat tab for Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users.
OpenAI says it reads photos better, follows instructions better when it searches the web, and can offer to watch a product for a price drop.
GPT-5.6 Sol will be retired on December 23.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI began rolling out a version of its GPT-6.2 Sol model to the Chat tab in ChatGPT on November 23, 2026. The company described this version as optimized for everyday conversation. It is going first to subscribers on the Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans, with a global rollout that starts gradually and may take a few days to reach every account.

The move came less than a week after GPT-6.2 first appeared in ChatGPT's Work tab and in Codex. OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on November 17, describing Sol as the model for everyday work and Astra as its frontier model for complex tasks. The models that power Work and Codex are not changing with this update, according to Digital Trends.
What the chat version does differently

According to 9to5Mac, the chat-tuned model is better at picking out details in photos, such as the symbols on a parking sign, and at following instructions when it searches the web. In one example the company gave, the model compared hotels by weighing a shorter walk against a lower nightly rate. It can also offer to alert a user when an item they are shopping for drops in price.

OpenAI published benchmark results from its own testing in the Chat tab. On image understanding, GPT-6.2 scored 71.7 percent, compared with 47.4 percent for GPT-6. On instruction following with challenging prompts, it scored 78.1 percent against 62.5 percent. iGeeksBlog also reported an internal BrowseComp result of 64.5 percent for GPT-6.2 at its highest thinking setting, up from 54.4 percent for GPT-6. All of these figures come from OpenAI rather than independent testers.

OpenAI also reported results from teen safety evaluations. According to iGeeksBlog, GPT-6.2 met the company's safety policies 91 to 94 percent of the time in challenging conversations, up from 77 to 80 percent for GPT-6, with gains in areas such as emotional reliance, dangerous activities and age-restricted goods.

In the model picker, the Latest option now uses GPT-6.2 across four thinking levels: Instant, Medium, High and Extra High, Digital Trends reported. The Pro thinking level still runs on GPT-6 Pro, because there is no GPT-6.2 Pro option yet. Enterprise access depends on settings chosen by each workspace administrator.
Free and Go users are not part of this rollout. According to iGeeksBlog, those plans continue to run on GPT-6 Luna in the Chat tab for now.
Two older models will be retired

OpenAI set December 23, 2026, as the retirement date for GPT-5.6 Sol. Paid users who still select it in the Chat tab can keep using it until then. GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Terra will also leave ChatGPT Work and Codex on the same day.

The update shows OpenAI moving its newest model family from professional tools into the part of ChatGPT that most subscribers use every day. Features such as price alerts point toward a chatbot that does small tasks on a user's behalf, not only one that answers questions. The gap between paid and free plans is also widening, since free users remain on an older model for everyday chat.
The next date to watch is December 23, when GPT-5.6 Sol and Terra are retired, along with any announcement about when free and Go users will get GPT-6.2 in the Chat tab.
